join_order.notes: Resolve rt_actress id via single-pass scan of role_type.role
Resolve it_rd id via single-pass scan of info_type.info
Build cn_us bitset of size company_name rows (dense PK) for O(1) company_id membership
name.gender is dense int8 array — direct index by pid-1
Test production_year[mv-1] > 2000 AND != INT32_MIN via dense PK direct lookup
For each candidate mv, iterate mi range [off[mv], off[mv+1]) testing info_type_id==it_rd; early-exit
For each candidate mv, iterate mc range [off[mv], off[mv+1]) testing cn_us[company_id-1]; early-exit
person_role_id != INT32_MIN is sufficient (FK to dense PK char_name.id)

filters.predicate: note IN (4 voice strings) AND role_id==rt_actress AND person_role_id!=INT32_MIN

data_structures.ci_note: string column with dictionary or direct compare against 4 voice literals
data_structures.min_aggregation: two scalar slots min(name), min(title) with thread-local then merge

parallelism.driver: cast_info linear scan partitioned into morsels of ~256K rows; thread-local min(name)/min(title); final reduction

strategy_notes: Drive from cast_info (36.2M rows) because the ci.note IN 4-voice-strings + role_id==rt_actress predicate is the most selective conjunction (~0.1% of ci rows). Apply cheap predicates first in this order to short-circuit: (1) role_id==rt_actress, (2) person_role_id!=INT32_MIN, (3) note IN voice-set, (4) name.gender==f via person_id lookup, (5) title.production_year>2000 via movie_id lookup, (6) mi release-dates existence, (7) mc [us] existence, (8) aka_name existence. Reorder cheapest-most-selective first. Resolved string dimension ids (rt_actress, it_rd, cc_us, g_f) at plan start so all inner-loop comparisons are integer. cn_us materialized as a bitset (~29KB) to fit in L1. All offsets/columns mmap'd; sequential scan of cast_info is HDD-friendly.
